**Proposed mechanism:** SEMA4A (HGNC:10728) —DISRUPTS→ Semaphorin signaling pathway (GO:0007237); SEMA7A (HGNC:10731) —DISRUPTS→ Semaphorin signaling pathway (GO:0007237); Semaphorin signaling pathway (GO:0007237) —LEADS_TO→ extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Retinitis pigmentosa (HP:0000547); extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Intrahepatic cholestasis (HP:0011310). **Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of semaphorin signaling and extracellular matrix organization in these two distinct diseases could reveal novel therapeutic targets for both retinitis pigmentosa and intrahepatic cholestasis, potentially through modulation of extracellular matrix homeostasis.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that the dysregulation of T-cell activation by PTPRC loss-of-function has no discernible impact on retinal cell development or function, or that SEMA4A dysfunction in retinal cells does not affect immune cell signaling pathways, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Identification of common variants (AF > 0.1%) in HGNC:10714 or HGNC:9070 that do not segregate with either disease phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared molecular underpinnings of these two distinct diseases could reveal novel therapeutic targets applicable to both immune disorders and neurodegenerative conditions affecting the retina. For instance, pathways regulating T-cell activation might influence glial cell function in the retina, or vice versa.
